To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new yeast surface display method to identify antibodies that bind and internalize into living cells.

we have identified a novel class of brain endothelial cell binding antibodies that can be used to probe brain endothelial cell biology and to target brain endothelium in the development of novel therapies for brain diseases.

we used a yeast display library to identify 34 unique human antibodies that bind to rat brain endothelial cell membranes, and we used a new immunoprecipitaion procedure to identify the cognate antigans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of yeast cell surface display technology for the discovery of new cell-binding antibodies.
the development of novel methods for the identification of cell-binding antibodies and the use of these methods to identify novel antigens.
the identification and characterization of brain endothelial cell-specific antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the yeast library was successfully used to mine for antibodies against a cell surface target, that a subset of these antibodies bound the target with high affinity, and that the yeast display immunopreservation procedure provided initial characterization of the antigen.

this work represents a successful proof of concept for the use of yeast display to identify antibodies that bind living brain endothelial cells, and that this approach can be used to identify new cell adhesion molecules.

the use of yeast display for cell surface screening can provide a rapid and efficient means to identify cell-binding antibodies and their cognate antigens, with the added benefit of identifying the antigen-binding domains of antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
yeast panning is an efficient and versatile method for identifying antibodies with affinity for a wide variety of cell-surface targets.

the yeast display system can be used to isolate antibodies that recognize a wide array of mammalian cell surface antigens and that the yeast display immunoprepitation procedure can be used to identify the corresponding antigen.
yeast surface display is a useful tool for the rapid identification of lead cell-binding antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
yeast display can be used to identify antibodies that bind to cell-surface molecules.

the yeast surface display system provides a powerful and versatile tool for the identification of novel human antibodies that bind and internalize into living cells, and that these antibodies may have potential for therapeutic use.

this approach can be used to identify antibodies that bind the cell surface of live brain endothelial cells, and that the antigens are amenable to further biochemical characterization using the new immunoprecipitations.
